gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a maker-sourced chart of which solar panel fits which camera generation. For example: Arlo's Pro (6th Gen) VMC4070 and Ultra (3rd Gen) VMC5050 are listed only for the VMA7600 Universal panel, not the magnetic VMA5600. The VMA3600 is for 1st-gen Essential only and the VMA6600 is for 2nd-gen Essential only. Ring's USB-C panel excludes the 1st-gen Stick Up Cam. Blink's Solar Panel Mount works only with Outdoor (3rd Gen) and not with Outdoor 4, XT or XT2. Reolink's 3/6/12 W panels fit every Reolink battery camera except the original Argus and Keen, and charge only from 0 to 45 °C.
standout_why: Compared against SafeWise (cited), Bob Vila (cited), rottenwifi best-solar-powered (cited) and homegearlab (cited); solargenadvisor (cited) would not load because of an SSL certificate error. SafeWise only says Arlo Essential needs 'the Arlo Essential Solar Panel Charger' and that Wyze Cam v3 can't use a panel. It names no model numbers, connectors or generations, and its picks are old (Argus 3 Pro, Arlo Pro 3). Homegearlab has one exclusion ('Blink's older Solar Panel Mount does not support the Outdoor 4') and gives a connector only for Ring (USB-C). Bob Vila and rottenwifi say nothing about connectors or generations. None of them lists the Arlo VMA panels by camera, Ring's barrel-plug adapter cases and the 1st-gen exclusion, Reolink's original Argus/Keen exclusion, its 0–45 °C charging window or its 9 m extension limit, or eufy's 3 W panel list. ChatGPT itself told shoppers to 'choose a panel explicitly compatible with your exact model' but named none.
decides: This mostly settles the second branch ChatGPT offered, 'just a solar panel for my existing camera'. The right panel is set by brand and generation, not by watts, and buying the wrong Arlo or Blink generation means a connector or mount that doesn't fit. It confirms Reolink's 6 W Solar Panel 2 (USB-C) as the right add-on for the Argus 4 Pro and Argus Eco Ultra that ChatGPT showed. For the eufy S340 and S3 Pro, it points to eufy's own 3 W panel ($29.99, sold as certified for both) rather than a third-party panel, because eufy warns non-certified panels may damage the battery. Ring Outdoor Cam/Spotlight owners can buy the $59.99 USB-C panel unless they own a 1st-gen Stick Up Cam.
